notes: One clear priority (loss of chest/spine inclination through impact) supported by a checkable head-centering observation and a finish-position description that a face-on camera can actually confirm, with a crisp belt-buckle/shirt-buttons feel.

"Arms look like they're doing a little more of the work than your torso" is an impression rather than a verifiable position, and the headline warns against hip sway immediately after stating the lower body stays centered, which muddies the diagnosis.

Names a specific phase (early takeaway), a specific geometric fault (club steep while torso stays quiet), and gives a genuinely checkable rehearsal test - shaft roughly matching shoulder angle at lead-arm-parallel.

Solid, committed, well-drilled lead-arm-width diagnosis with a clear radius mechanism, but its checkpoint ("hands farther from your chest than they are now") is relative and eyeballed rather than measurable against any reference.

Confident, concrete setup fix, but the load-bearing claim that the ball sits "well ahead of your lead foot" is close to unreadable from a backlit down-the-line frame where stance-length position is foreshortened, and the fault as described would be a freak setup - the one-line lighting caveat does not cover it.

Anchors the fault to a self-referencing baseline - club at the top high and upright relative to where the shaft started - which is exactly the kind of comparison a backlit silhouette can support, plus a centered-head observation and a waist-high rehearsal.

Specific top-of-swing description (arms folded, lead elbow softening, hands close to head) with a sound radius-to-low-point mechanism and a well-dosed drill, but all of it is joint-position language with no angular reference a coach could measure.

"Shaft well above the angle it started on" plus the clubhead-over-hands checkpoint at lead-arm-parallel are both verifiable from video, and the closing "keep that as the only thought" is the strongest single-priority commitment in the set.
